lead.headline: MoonPay's bank charter bid and CFTC's Hyperliquid roadmap signal US crypto banking convergence
lead.tldr: Today's signals point to a structural repricing of crypto infrastructure around regulated US access: MoonPay is underwriting its payments stack on a national trust bank, while the CFTC is drawing the compliance path for onchain derivatives venues. The throughline is that regulatory clarity is becoming a balance-sheet asset, not a lobbying outcome.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today's brief tracks how US regulatory scaffolding is hardening into competitive moats for crypto-native firms willing to pay the compliance cost of entry.

top_signals.title: Binance hackers stole 192 tokens across 11 networks, court docs show
top_signals.summary: Court documents have revealed detailed specifics regarding a massive $6.3 billion hack of Binance. The theft involved 192 different tokens across 11 networks, including over $3.46 billion in stablecoins.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The scale of the Binance hack—$6.3 billion across 192 tokens—exposes how cross-chain complexity has outpaced security underwriting, and custodians will face repricing pressure as insurers and LPs recalibrate counterparty risk models.

top_signals.title: MoonPay seeks US bank charter for stablecoin, custody services
top_signals.summary: MoonPay is seeking federal approval to establish a national trust bank based in Miami. This move aims to integrate stablecoin and custody services directly into a regulated US banking framework.
top_signals.why_it_matters: MoonPay's national trust bank pursuit represents a direct arbitrage on the gap between crypto-native UX and FDIC-regulated plumbing, positioning it to capture spreads that currently leak to correspondent banking layers.

top_signals.title: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
top_signals.summary: SEC nominee Kristin Johnson has expressed support for establishing formal rulemaking to govern the trading of tokenized stocks. Additionally, Steven Levine highlighted the agency's ability to provide exemptions for such activities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Johnson's endorsement of formal rulemaking for tokenized equities signals that the SEC is moving from enforcement-driven ambiguity to codified exemptions, which would let broker-dealers underwrite tokenized securities with defined capital requirements.

top_signals.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could slip to May 2027 over compatibility concerns
top_signals.summary: The Ethereum Glamsterdam upgrade may be delayed until May 2027 due to potential smart contract compatibility issues. Developers are concerned that the update could negatively impact at least 50 companies.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A two-year Glamsterdam delay would freeze Ethereum's execution roadmap while competitors iterate, forcing institutional commitments to be repriced against Solana and other chains with more predictable upgrade cycles.

top_signals.title: CFTC Chair Selig outlines how Hyperliquid and other onchain venues could enter the US
top_signals.summary: CFTC Chair Selig provided a regulatory roadmap for onchain venues like Hyperliquid to legally offer derivatives to U.S. retail traders. He specified that such platforms must either register as an exchange or partner with an existing registered entity.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Selig's dual-path framework—register or partner—creates a tiered market where compliant onchain venues can access US retail flow at structural margin advantages over offshore operators operating in regulatory gray zones.

on_the_radar.title: US launches cybercrime center with TRM Labs to help trace crypto tied to scams
on_the_radar.summary: The US government has launched the Threat Disruption Center in partnership with TRM Labs to combat crypto-related scams. The center aims to facilitate information sharing between investigators and technology companies to trace and disrupt illicit digital asset flows.

on_the_radar.title: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement between tokenized deposits and money market funds
on_the_radar.summary: Ant International has launched the Whale Orchestration Protocol as part of Singapore's MAS BLOOM initiative. The protocol enables real-time settlement between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds.

on_the_radar.title: Singapore settles $77.5M tokenized bill sale with wholesale CBDC
on_the_radar.summary: Singapore has successfully settled a $77.5 million tokenized bill sale using a wholesale CBDC. The transaction took place on the Singapore Dollar Test Network, which the MAS intends to rename the SG Digital Ledger.

on_the_radar.title: Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
on_the_radar.summary: Hong Kong's securities regulator has added the crypto platform Hyperliquid to its 'Alert List'. The move comes amid allegations that the platform has been offering digital asset trading services without the required license.

on_the_radar.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
on_the_radar.summary: Institutional holdings of Bitcoin Exchange Traded Products (ETPs) have reached a new all-time high. Data from 13F filings indicate that the wealth channel now accounts for 40% of ETP ownership.

on_the_radar.title: 1inch integrates Hyperliquid's perpetual futures contracts into its dApp and wallet platform
on_the_radar.summary: 1inch has integrated Hyperliquid's perpetual futures contracts into its dApp and wallet platform. This allows users to fund trading positions using tokens held on 1inch, which are then routed to USDC for deposit on Hyperliquid.

on_the_radar.title: IOSCO warns quantum upgrades could slow blockchains, leave security gaps
on_the_radar.summary: The global securities regulator IOSCO has issued a warning regarding the transition to quantum-resistant blockchain technology. The organization suggests that these upgrades could potentially degrade network performance and create security vulnerabilities in wallets and layer-2 systems.

on_the_radar.title: Senators warn GENIUS Act rules could push stablecoin firms toward federal oversight
on_the_radar.summary: Six US senators have expressed concern that the proposed GENIUS Act rules may unfairly favor federally regulated stablecoin issuers. They are urging the Treasury to ensure that state-level issuers receive similar protections to maintain a balanced regulatory landscape.

worth_a_read.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's data on ETP inflows provides the demand-side counterweight to the treasury-side rate sensitivity flagged in today's funding candidate, letting analysts triangulate whether institutional BTC accumulation is accelerating or merely rotating.

worth_a_read.title: Gate Money: From Exchange to Neobank
worth_a_read.note: Messari's exchange-to-neobank framing directly contextualizes MoonPay's charter strategy, mapping how crypto firms are repricing their revenue stacks from trading fees to net-interest-margin and deposit franchise value.

linkedin_post:
MoonPay wants to be a bank. Not a fintech with a sponsor bank. A national trust bank, Miami-based, holding its own stablecoin reserves and custody books on its own balance sheet.

We've watched crypto firms chase banking partnerships for a decade. The model was always rent the license, hide in the stack, hope the sponsor doesn't get skittish. MoonPay is betting that's exhausted. The CFTC's Selig gave the other half of this story today: a compliance roadmap for Hyperliquid and its peers to serve US retail legally. The condition is registration or partnership with a registered exchange. Either path requires balance-sheet depth and regulatory infrastructure that looks a lot like what MoonPay is building.

What we're underwriting here is whether regulated access becomes the scarce asset in crypto infrastructure. If it does, the firms that paid the compliance cost early—real capital requirements, real examination cycles, real legal entity structuring—capture spreads that offshore venues cannot match. The repricing is from technology risk to regulatory execution risk.

The test: in twelve months, does a registered onchain venue command a valuation premium over a comparable offshore operator? Or does the US retail user simply not care?
